Hotpot alt · Shu Daxia.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers report 40 min to 2 h waits at Shu Daxia peak dinner (18:00–21:00) on top of a ~1.5–2 h table sitting.

Land at CTU.basis: Chengdu Shuangliu arrival guides say domestic arrivals skip immigration and advise meeters to turn up ~30 min after touchdown.

Check in at Minyoun Dongda.basis: Standard China 4–5 star check-in with passport registration plus getting bags to the room; 24/7 front desk so no wait for staff.

Dinner.basis: Ordinary (non-hotpot) Chinese sit-down dinner runs about 1.5 h once ordering, shared dishes and paying are included.

Taikoo Li.basis: Chengdu guides put a relaxed walk through Taikoo Li at 1–2 hours, longer only if you stop to dine.

Daci Temple.basis: Trip.com itinerary allows about an hour for the halls; the compound is small and free, so 45 min covers halls plus the relic room without tea.

IFS rooftop panda.basis: Trip reports note a line forms for close-up photos with the climbing panda even at mall opening, but the terrace itself is one small garden.

Breakfast.basis: Standard unhurried hotel buffet breakfast in China before an early departure.

Chengdu Panda Base.basis: Guides advise at least 3–4 h because the base is large; walking the whole park is about 3 h, and 2.5 h is described on TripAdvisor as the rushed minimum.

Lunch.basis: Standard mid-trip Chinese restaurant lunch — order, eat, pay in about an hour.

Chengdu Museum.basis: Reviewers report 2 h for a leisurely pass and 3–4 h for the full building; 2.5 h covers the history floors plus the shadow-puppet gallery.

People’s Park.basis: Guides bundle park plus teahouse into 1–2 h; with Heming timed separately, the lake loop and marriage-market corner take about 45 min.

Heming Teahouse.basis: Teahouse sources put the average Heming visit at 1–2 h with no table time limit, and caier ear cleaning adds roughly 20–30 min.

Kuanzhai Alleys.basis: TripAdvisor and Chinese guides recommend 2–3 h for the wide, narrow and well lanes, best from about 17:00 once the lights come on.

Sichuan opera.basis: Shufeng Yayun runs nightly from 20:00 for 80–90 min, with a 19:30 arrival for seating, tea and backstage face-painting.

Chengdu East → Guanghan.basis: Rail guides advise 30–40 min inside Chengdu East for security and ID checks before the ~18 min high-speed hop to Guanghan North.

Hotpot alt · Lao Matou.basis: TripAdvisor reviewer of Lao Matou Yulin waited 90 min then ate for an hour; a mid-evening arrival at this less touristy branch lands nearer 30–45 min queue plus ~1.5 h at table.

Guanghan North.basis: Small suburban station — walk out and join the taxi/shuttle rank; the 15–20 min ride to the museum is travel, not stop time.

Sanxingdui Museum.n: New hall plus old bronze hall
Sanxingdui Museum.basis: Official and tour guidance since the 2023 new building recommends 3–4 h (some say 3–5 h) for the new halls plus the old bronze hall; it is genuinely a half-day.

SKP Chengdu.basis: Visitors describe SKP as a photo/architecture stop rather than a shopping trip — five sunken floors and the rooftop garden take about an hour to walk.

Wuhou Shrine.basis: Chengdu guides state the main sights take about two hours, three if you linger in the gardens or the Three Kingdoms history.

Jinli Old Street.basis: Guides suggest 2–3 h for Jinli at sunset; 1.5 h fits a walk plus snacks when Wuhou Shrine next door is visited the same evening.

Head to Chengdu East.basis: Guidance for Chengdu East, the region's busiest station, is to arrive 30–60 min before departure for security, ID gates and finding the platform; the 45–60 min transfer is travel, not stop time.
